attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT/egress gateway for node2 and node3 (Alpine), entirely via an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the pre-installed control node): node1's eth0 (10.100.7.10/24, shared with node2/node3) got a static IP, a default route to the platform gateway (10.100.7.1), and a source-NAT masquerade rule for 10.100.7.0/24 outbound eth0; node2/node3's dhcpcd config was overridden to route their default gateway through node1 instead of the platform gateway directly. Verified via conntrack/nftables counters that node2/node3 traffic is genuinely translated through node1, then completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes, confirming boot-id changes and full recovery of NAT, routing, and Ansible/SSH connectivity after each restart.
